result.label: bug
result.what_to_change: The readiness handler only returns HTTP 503 when status is "down"; a "degraded" queue (depth > QUEUE_DEGRADED_AT) still yields HTTP 200, so load-balancer probes that key off the status code can't distinguish healthy from degraded. The status-to-HTTP-code mapping should give degraded a non-200 (or otherwise distinct) response, or the endpoint should document/expose a code probes can use to take the instance out of rotation.
result.evidence: src/api/health.ts: `res.status(status === "down" ? 503 : 200).json({ status, ... })` — only "down" triggers 503; when checks.queue is "degraded" the computed status is "degraded" but the response is still 200, matching the exact symptom in the issue (200 with status/queue "degraded").

could_not_determine: Whether the intended fix is to change the HTTP status code mapping or instead to document the expected probe behavior (policy decision not resolved by the code alone)
